data.title: Gold and Silver Hit 14-Month Lows as Selling Pressure Intensifies
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • Gold has lost around 15% from its early November peak. Silver has fallen by a similar amount since last Friday.
  • Silver’s faster decline lifted the gold-to-silver ratio to about 85, its highest level in more than a year.
  • Higher US yields, a stronger dollar and expectations of further Fed rate hikes drove the initial sell-off. Gold fell faster even as those pressures eased.
  • The relative strength index has dropped deep into oversold territory for both metals, increasing the scope for a short-term rebound.
  • Lower prices are drawing physical buyers in China and India, while ETF flows will show whether investment demand is also improving.

Gold’s decline accelerates as the dollar steadies

The initial sell-off in gold followed a familiar pattern. US Treasury yields rose, the dollar strengthened and hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve officials led investors to price in further rate hikes. Higher yields increased the opportunity cost of holding bullion, which pays no interest. A stronger dollar added pressure by making gold more expensive for buyers using other currencies.

Over the past few days, Treasury yields gave back some of their gains, the dollar steadied and expectations for Fed policy changed little. Gold’s decline nevertheless accelerated. One possible explanation is that another round of losses in technology stocks prompted investors to sell bullion to raise cash. Investors who need liquidity can sell gold alongside equities, even when the broader market mood would ordinarily favour demand for safe-haven assets. That may help explain why the latest leg of the sell-off was so sharp.

Silver underperforms as the gold-to-silver ratio climbs

Silver fell to just above $41 an ounce overnight. It lost roughly as much in less than a week as gold did in nearly two weeks. That pushed the gold-to-silver ratio to around 85, meaning one ounce of gold bought about 85 ounces of silver, the most in more than a year.

The ratio is worth watching if prices begin to recover. A decline from these levels would mean silver is regaining ground against gold. If both metals rebound while the ratio remains elevated, gold would still be leading the recovery.

Oversold RSI flags room for a short-term rebound

The relative strength index, or RSI, has fallen deep into oversold territory for both metals. The indicator measures the strength of recent price moves, and the low readings reflect how persistent the selling has been. Similar episodes have often preceded short-term rebounds as selling pressure faded. The RSI can stay oversold during a sustained decline, so the first indication of stabilisation would come from prices themselves, for example if another round of selling fails to produce fresh lows.

The macro backdrop will also matter. A rebound would have a better chance of gaining traction if the dollar and Treasury yields stay below their recent highs and investors hold off on pricing in more Fed tightening. Renewed gains in yields or the dollar could limit the recovery, especially if the market starts to expect a larger cumulative increase in US rates.

Asian physical demand firms as ETF flows come into Focus

The sell-off is already drawing physical buyers in China and India. Local gold premiums in India roughly doubled over the past week amid wedding-season demand, while premiums in China traded around $10 an ounce. Those premiums measure how much local buyers are paying above the international benchmark. Their rise as global prices fall suggests that lower prices are bringing some buyers back into the market.

ETF flows will offer a read on whether financial investors are responding in the same way. Fresh inflows would show that investors are willing to rebuild exposure after the sell-off and could help sustain a rebound. Continued redemptions could keep prices under pressure, particularly if investors are still cutting positions to free up cash. The strongest sign of a more durable recovery would be an improvement in ETF flows alongside firmer physical demand and a stabilisation in US yields and the dollar.

data.title: FOMC meeting minutes, gold outlook and technical analysis
data.description:
Referenced assets

Key takeaways

  • Upcoming FOMC minutes: The Federal Reserve is set to release minutes from its October 27–28 meeting, where rates were held steady at 3.75%–4% in a 10-2 vote. Traders will analyze the text for the breadth of support behind dissenter calls for rate hikes and signals regarding potential policy tightening in December.
  • Gold technical downtrend: Gold remains in a firm weekly downtrend within a descending channel, having fallen 31% from its peak near 5,400. The loss and subsequent rejection of the 2023 multi-year uptrend line near 4,000–4,050 suggests old support has flipped to key dynamic resistance.
  • Bearish technical bias & levels: Technical indicators (9/21 EMA bearish crossover, RSI at 34.95, expanding negative MACD histogram) favor continued downside toward lower channel support around 3,640–3,700. Bullish invalidation requires a weekly close above resistance at 4,330–4,350.

On Wednesday at 2:00 pm ET, the Federal Reserve is scheduled to publish the minutes from its October 27–28 meeting. While the initial statement confirmed that interest rates were held steady at 3.75%–4%, these minutes will reveal the extent of the debate regarding potential rate increases.

The decision to maintain rates was made on a 10-2 vote, with dissents from Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Governor Lisa Cook, who both favored a 25-basis-point rate hike. Additionally, the official statement revised its assessment of economic expansion from “solid” to “strong”. Taken together, these developments underscore an active internal discussion about further policy tightening.

Whereas the post-meeting statement and press conference with Chair Kevin Warsh provided high-level summaries, the upcoming minutes offer the first comprehensive record of how all committee members weighed opposing arguments.

Key considerations for the upcoming minutes

  • Minutes are backward-looking, since the meeting was three weeks ago, so reactions are usually modest unless the language differs from what traders expected.
  • The Fed met on October 27–28, before the October jobs report (November 6) and the October CPI (November 10), so the minutes reflect the committee’s view ahead of both releases.
  • When reviewing the minutes, key areas of focus include assessing how many officials supported the dissenters—where terms like “many” or “most” would signal a stronger shift toward a rate hike—and evaluating whether inflation is seen as persistent, broadening, or driven by upside risks like energy, tariffs, or labor costs.
  • Additionally, market participants will look for guidance on December, specifically conditional language indicating an appetite for further policy tightening in response to incoming data.
  • As of November 18, shortly ahead of the release, CME FedWatch indicates a 100% probability of a rate increase at the December 9 meeting, with a 95.0% chance of a 25-basis-point hike and a 5.0% chance of a 50-basis-point move.

Gold weekly chart technical analysis

Overview

  • The market is in a clear weekly downtrend. After a parabolic run from the 2023 uptrend to a peak near 5,400 in March 2026, price has fallen about 31%. It has now broken the multi-year support line and is trading at the lower end of a descending channel.
  • The late-January “exhaustion gap” marked the top. Price spiked to roughly 5,600, then reversed hard in March with a large bearish candle. Since then, it has made lower highs (about 4,700 in August and about 4,150 in November) and lower lows within a descending channel drawn from the March high.
  • The 2023 uptrend line (blue) held throughout the entire advance and was lost from late October to early November. Price retested it from below in the first week of November, around 4,000–4,050, and was rejected. The current weekly candle is a large bearish candle closing below the channel midpoint. That rejection turns the old support into resistance. The lower channel boundary sits near 3,640–3,700, so price is almost at it.

Indicators

  • Price is below the 9 EMA (4,010.7). The 9/21 crossover shows the fast average (4,039) below the slow one (4,176), a bearish cross that has held since the autumn. Both are sloping down and act as dynamic resistance.
  • RSI is 34.95, below its own average (44.94) and below 50 since March. It is approaching but not yet at oversold (30), so there is room for further downside. The failed rallies each stalled below 60, which is possible in a bear market.
  • The MACD line (−131.5) is below the signal line (−84.4) and below zero. The histogram (−47.2) is expanding again. The brief bullish cross in August failed near the zero line, and the new bearish cross confirms the move.

Conclusion

The base case is bearish. A weekly close below S1 and the channel floor (about 3,700) would open S2 at 3,634 and then S3 at 3,398. Because price is near the channel floor and RSI is nearing oversold, a short-term bounce toward 3,829 is possible. That would more likely be a pullback within the downtrend than a reversal, unless price holds above it.

A bullish shift would need a weekly close back above 3,829 and 3,991. A close above the 9 EMA (about 4,010) and the broken trendline would follow. Full invalidation of the bearish view would require a break of the upper channel and R2, around 4,330–4,350.

data.title: Anthropic’s IPO: A make-or-break test for the trillion-dollar AI trade
data.description:
Referenced assets

Key takeaways

  • Anthropic’s IPO is reportedly six times oversubscribed, according to Bloomberg on 12 November, reinforcing the positive sentiment surrounding the AI investment theme ahead of its anticipated Nasdaq debut on 19 November 2026.
  • Its indicative valuation of up to US$1.4 trillion faces a significant fundamental test, given US$900.9 billion in multi-year AI infrastructure commitments and signs of moderating quarterly revenue growth.
  • A sustained post-IPO share price decline could trigger a broader reassessment of AI-related equity valuations, particularly if accompanied by relative weakness in semiconductor stocks, deteriorating Nasdaq 100 market breadth and widening credit spreads.

Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO) has reportedly attracted demand equivalent to approximately six times the shares available, according to a Bloomberg report published on Thursday, 12 November 2026. The strong institutional response emerged just two days after the AI developer officially launched its IPO marketing campaign on 10 November.

At the upper end of its indicative US$70–US$78 price range, Anthropic is seeking to raise approximately US$64.4 billion by selling 825 million shares, potentially valuing the company at around US$1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

The offering is expected to be priced on Wednesday,18 November 2026, ahead of its anticipated Nasdaq trading debut under the ticker ANT on Thursday, 19 November 2026. These dates remain subject to the final offering timetable.

The reported six-times oversubscription suggests that institutional investors remain willing to commit substantial capital to the AI investment theme, despite recent concerns over elevated technology stock valuations and the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending.

More importantly, the strong order book may create a near-term demand imbalance in the secondary market.

Institutional investors receiving smaller-than-requested IPO allocations could seek additional shares after listing, potentially reinforcing an initial rally in Anthropic's share price.

This positive feedback loop may be amplified by expectations of passive investment inflows. Reuters reported on 12 November that Anthropic could attract approximately US$19 billion in index-related demand, subject to the company’s eventual eligibility for major equity benchmarks.

However, a heavily oversubscribed IPO does not guarantee sustained aftermarket strength. Some orders may be revised before allocation, and limited initial availability of shares can temporarily exaggerate price movements in either direction.

Hence, Anthropic’s post-listing performance, rather than the strength of its IPO order book alone, will provide a more meaningful assessment of underlying market conviction towards the AI investment theme.

US$900.9 billion in infrastructure commitments raises the hurdle for sustaining its premium valuation

Despite the strong IPO demand, Anthropic’s latest financial disclosures highlight a potential divergence between rapid revenue expansion and the substantial capital required to sustain its AI infrastructure development.

According to its amended SEC registration statement dated 10 November 2026, Anthropic disclosed approximately US$900.9 billion in aggregate computing and infrastructure commitments over multiple years, including US$451.6 billion expected through 2030.

Of these commitments, approximately US$70.7 billion falls due within the subsequent 12 months.

These figures represent contractual commitments over different time horizons rather than an immediate financing shortfall.

Anthropic also reported approximately US$146.6 billion in available liquidity as of 30 September 2026, comprising cash, short-term investments and undrawn credit facilities.

In addition, the company has arranged a US$26 billion private placement involving major technology firms, including Google, Nvidia and AMD, highlighting the growing financial interconnectedness between AI model developers and their infrastructure suppliers.

While these financing arrangements may alleviate immediate liquidity concerns, they do not eliminate the longer-term challenge of generating sufficient operating cash flow to support future infrastructure commitments.

More importantly, the reliance on strategic technology investors raises questions about the extent to which investment flows within the AI ecosystem are supporting demand for computing infrastructure.

If AI monetisation disappoints, a reduction in capital commitments by frontier model developers could subsequently weaken revenue expectations for semiconductor manufacturers, data-centre operators and cloud infrastructure providers.

Revenue growth remains strong, but a slowdown in its quarterly momentum warrants attention

Anthropic’s Q3 2026 revenue reached approximately US$17 billion, an increase of 47% quarter-on-quarter, compared with the much stronger growth rate of 144% recorded in Q2.

The company also disclosed an annualised revenue run rate of approximately US$81 billion as of October 2026, reinforcing expectations of continued commercial adoption of its Claude AI models.

Nevertheless, its indicative fully diluted valuation of US$1.4 trillion implies approximately 17.3 times its October annualised revenue run rate.

This is a run-rate valuation multiple, not a trailing-12-month price-to-sales ratio.

Such a premium valuation suggests that a substantial portion of future revenue growth and profitability improvements may already be reflected in the IPO price.

Against this backdrop, moderating revenue growth, weaker operating leverage or disappointing free cash flow generation could trigger a reassessment of Anthropic’s valuation, even if its underlying business continues to expand.

The key question for traders and investors is therefore whether incremental revenue growth can generate sufficient increases in operating cash flow and returns on invested capital to justify the company’s substantial infrastructure obligations.

Anthropic’s own investor materials show that revenue relative to computing and infrastructure costs declined from 2.08 times in Q2 to 1.72 times in Q3, partly due to the use of more expensive short-term computing capacity. (see Fig.1).

Hence, strong revenue growth alone may no longer be sufficient to sustain premium AI equity valuations if capital productivity fails to improve.

Could Anthropic’s post-IPO share price performance derail the trillion-dollar AI trade?

Anthropic’s anticipated Nasdaq debut could become a significant sentiment indicator for AI-related equities, particularly given its substantial valuation and commercial relationships with major technology companies.

A successful listing, accompanied by sustained share price appreciation, may reinforce risk appetite towards semiconductor stocks, cloud infrastructure providers and the broader Nasdaq 100.

However, a sharp reversal after an initially strong debut could send a different signal.

Such a development would suggest that the positive market response was driven predominantly by short-term IPO allocation constraints, momentum-driven buying and anticipated index-related inflows, rather than a sustainable reassessment of Anthropic’s earnings and cash flow prospects.

This could undermine investor confidence in the broader AI investment narrative through three transmission channels.

First, valuation compression across AI-related equities. A sustained decline in Anthropic shares below the final IPO price could encourage market participants to reassess the premium valuation multiples assigned to companies with substantial exposure to AI revenue growth.

Second, heightened concerns over circular AI financing. Anthropic’s strategic financing relationships with major infrastructure suppliers may increase scrutiny of the financial interdependencies across the AI ecosystem. If investors begin questioning the sustainability of infrastructure demand, the negative feedback loop could extend to semiconductor suppliers and cloud service providers.

Third, a broader deterioration in risk appetite. Should Anthropic’s post-IPO weakness coincide with declining semiconductor relative strength, worsening Nasdaq 100 market breadth and rising technology-sector volatility, it would increase the risk of a wider corrective decline across US equities.

Post-IPO trading scenarios: The pivotal price reference will be Anthropic’s final offer price

With Anthropic yet to establish a public trading history, conventional technical indicators such as its 20-day, 50-day and 200-day moving averages are unavailable.

Hence, the final IPO offer price, opening trading range and initial volume-weighted average price (VWAP) will provide the first meaningful reference levels for assessing its near-term price structure.

The following are illustrative monitoring thresholds, not statistically derived price targets.

Scenario Anthropic share price structure Broader AI market implications
Bullish continuation Sustained trading above the IPO offer price, potentially exceeding it by 20% Reinforces positive sentiment and may support renewed buying across AI infrastructure equities
Consolidation Trading largely within 10% above or below the IPO offer price Suggests initial enthusiasm is normalising, with investors refocusing on earnings and valuation fundamentals
Bearish reversal A sustained decline of at least 20% below the IPO offer price Increases the risk of broader AI valuation repricing, particularly if confirmed by semiconductor underperformance

A particularly concerning technical development would be an initial price surge followed by a reversal below the IPO offer price within the first several trading sessions.

Such a move could signal weakening demand after initial allocation-driven buying has subsided.

A subsequent failed recovery above the IPO price would reinforce the bearish tone and increase the odds of further selling pressure.

On the other hand, sustained trading above the initial opening range, accompanied by strong volume and relative strength in the semiconductor sector, would suggest that institutional demand remains supportive.

In addition, we can roughly gauge current short-term sentiment toward Anthropic’s IPO via its pre-IPO perpetual futures contract, which is settled in stablecoins such as USDC and listed on a decentralised exchange (see Fig. 2).

Technical analysis on Anthropic’s pre-IPO perps: Downward trend below 103.20

Based on the current price ($101.72) of its pre-IPO perpetual futures on a per-share basis (ANT/USDC) on Hyperliquid at the time of writing, it is trading at around a 30% premium to the upper end of the expected $78.00 IPO price (see Fig. 2).

Despite the current absolute premium of 30%, its short-term price action has shifted into a minor downtrend, with price oscillating within a descending channel since the 11 November 2026 high of 107.93, which suggests an increasing risk of near-term downside pressure.

A break below 100.70 exposes the next intermediate supports at 98.88 and 96.91/96.26.

On the flip side, a clearance above 103.20, a key short-term pivotal resistance, invalidates the bearish bias, with the next intermediate resistance coming in at 105.28 and 107.00/107.93.

data.title: The US labour market is losing momentum – as is the USD
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • The U.S. labor market is losing momentum, but not collapsing. Nonfarm payrolls rose by only 57,000, previous months were revised lower, and hiring has clearly slowed, while layoffs remain limited.
  • The drop in unemployment is less positive than it looks. The unemployment rate fell to 4.2%, but this was partly due to a decline in labor force participation to 61.5%, meaning some people stopped actively looking for work.
  • The report reduced pressure on the Fed to tighten policy further. Slower job growth and easing wage pressure revived hopes for future rate cuts, weakened the dollar, and supported assets such as gold, Bitcoin, and EUR/USD.

June data from the U.S. labor market showed a clear weakening in employment momentum. Nonfarm payrolls increased by only 57,000, significantly below economists’ expectations. In addition, data for the previous two months were revised downward, weakening earlier signals that had suggested greater resilience in the labor market.

At first glance, the decline in the unemployment rate to 4.2% appeared positive. However, this is not an unambiguous sign of improvement. The drop in unemployment was accompanied by a marked decline in labor force participation. The participation rate fell to 61.5%, reaching its lowest level in more than five years. This means that some individuals stopped actively looking for work and were therefore no longer included in unemployment statistics.

Companies are not conducting mass layoffs, but they are hiring more cautiously

The report does not point to a labor market collapse, but it does show increasing caution among employers. Initial jobless claims remained almost unchanged, suggesting that the scale of layoffs remains limited. The issue, therefore, is not a sharp reduction in employment, but a weaker willingness among companies to create new jobs.

The largest decline in employment was recorded in the leisure and hospitality sector. This is particularly important because, at this time of year, the industry typically increases seasonal hiring. Weaker-than-usual employment growth may indicate a more cautious approach by companies toward consumer demand and future operating costs.

At the same time, some sectors continued to support the labor market. Healthcare and social assistance remained the main source of employment growth. Job numbers also increased in manufacturing and construction. Weakness persisted, however, in the information sector, where employment declined for the seventeenth time in the past eighteen months.

Wages are rising, but inflationary pressure is easing

Average hourly earnings rose by 3.5% year over year in June. This increase shows that wages are still growing, but they are no longer generating inflationary pressure as strong as during the period of peak labor market tightness. For the Federal Reserve, this may be an argument that employment conditions remain relatively stable and do not require an abrupt policy response.

From the perspective of households, however, the picture is less favorable. Slower employment growth means fewer opportunities to find a new job, while inflation continues to limit the real purchasing power of wages. Even if nominal wages are rising, many workers may not feel a clear improvement in their financial situation.

Markets took note of the report’s weakness

The release triggered a moderately positive reaction in financial markets. The S&P 500 opened higher, while U.S. Treasury yields declined. Investors scaled back expectations for further interest rate hikes by the Fed, although they still priced in at least one rate increase this year.

The market reaction shows that weaker employment data were interpreted as a factor reducing pressure on the central bank. If the labor market continues to lose momentum, the Fed may have fewer reasons to tighten monetary policy further.

A mixed picture of the U.S. economy

The data were disappointing, but they should not fundamentally change the overall assessment of the economy. The labor market reflects uneven economic growth, in which some sectors are still creating jobs while others are clearly slowing. From the Fed’s perspective, the situation does not look alarming, as the labor market is not generating additional inflationary pressure. For American households, however, it means more difficult conditions, especially when limited employment opportunities coincide with persistently high living costs.

Kevin Warsh’s first press conference as FOMC Chair was perceived as hawkish and fueled concerns about an interest rate hike in the United States. As a result, the dollar strengthened significantly in recent weeks. Following today’s NFP report, hopes for an interest rate cut have resurfaced. Of course, with core PCE inflation currently at 3.4% year over year, this remains unlikely. Nevertheless, today’s reading creates a balance between arguments for monetary easing and monetary tightening, given the Fed’s dual mandate of maximum employment and price stability. It was precisely these hopes that led to a weakening of the dollar. EUR/USD is currently trading at 1.1446, up 0.59%. Instruments quoted in USD, which have recently failed to generate returns for investors, also deserve attention. Gold is up 2.37% today, while Bitcoin has gained 2.64%.

A labor market without collapse, but also without strength

The June report shows that the U.S. labor market is in a phase of clear slowdown. There are no signs of mass layoffs or a sharp deterioration in conditions, but it is becoming increasingly difficult to describe the market as strong. Companies are acting cautiously, new jobs are being created more slowly, and the decline in unemployment is partly the result of lower labor force participation.

The key takeaway from the report is therefore that the labor market is not collapsing, but it is losing resilience. For the Fed, this means less pressure from wages and employment, while for workers it means more challenging job-search conditions and limited improvement in real incomes.

data.title: Bitcoin Deepens Losses - Crypto Market Under Pressure
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • Bitcoin is under strong selling pressure, falling over 17% in a week and dropping below USD 60,000. The decline was intensified by USD 532 million in long liquidations on Binance, which triggered additional forced selling.
  • Market sentiment worsened after Strategy sold part of its bitcoin holdings. Although the sale was small — 32 BTC for USD 2.5 million — it raised concerns that the largest corporate bitcoin holder could make further sales in the future.
  • The broader crypto market is weak due to macro and demand concerns. Strong U.S. labor data reduced hopes for rate cuts, retail investors are shifting toward AI-related tech stocks, ETF inflows remain too small to support prices, and security concerns after the Zcash vulnerability further damaged trust.

Bitcoin has come under heavy selling pressure and has already lost more than 17 percent since the beginning of the week. On Friday, its price fell below the psychological barrier of USD 60,000, increasing investor concerns about a further deepening of the correction. Bitcoin has fallen below its 200-week SMA for the first time in three years. From its all-time high near USD 126,000, the leading cryptocurrency has already lost more than half of its value.

Long liquidations increase pressure on the market

The scale of the declines was amplified by the forced closure of leveraged positions. Over the past 24 hours, long positions worth USD 532 million were liquidated on the Binance exchange. Such a large wave of liquidations shows that many investors betting on a bitcoin rebound were forced to close their positions, which further increased selling pressure in the market.

This mechanism often deepens declines, as automatic liquidations lead to further sell orders. As a result, the market can move more sharply than would be implied solely by incoming macroeconomic data or the decisions of the largest investors.

Strategy’s Bitcoin sale weighed on sentiment

One of the factors worsening sentiment was the news that Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin and a company associated with Michael Saylor, had sold part of its bitcoin holdings. The company sold 32 bitcoins for USD 2.5 million. Although the transaction was small compared with the company’s overall portfolio, it carried significant symbolic weight.

It was only Strategy’s second bitcoin sale since it began making purchases in 2020. The company explained the decision as necessary to pay coupons to holders of preferred shares, but investors interpreted it as a possible weakening of the long-standing narrative of holding bitcoin indefinitely.

The market is primarily concerned that this small sale could foreshadow further, larger transactions in the future. This risk was highlighted by Peter Schiff, a well-known bitcoin critic, who stressed that the problem is not the scale of the current sale itself, but its potential consequences for investor confidence. Before this transaction, Strategy had reportedly purchased a total of 843,738 BTC for nearly USD 64 billion, which is why any change in the company’s strategy is being closely watched by the market.

Declines spread across the entire cryptocurrency market

Selling pressure was not limited to bitcoin. Ethereum fell by around 23 percent over the week to USD 1,555, while Solana lost about 22 percent, dropping to USD 63.75. Weakness was also visible in shares of companies linked to cryptocurrencies. Strategy’s stock fell by almost 10 percent, while Coinbase shares declined by 8.4 percent.

A modest positive signal came from inflows into U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs yesterday after 13 days of outflows. However, the scale of these inflows, amounting to just over USD 3 million, was too small to change the overall market picture. In practice, this means that institutional demand remains too weak to effectively stop the current sell-off.

Strong U.S. Data reduces hopes for rate cuts

Sentiment was also hurt by strong data from the U.S. labor market. Nonfarm payrolls rose by 172,000 in May, clearly above expectations. Such data reduces the likelihood of swift interest rate cuts in the United States, which is unfavorable for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.

The strong labor market report weakened the narrative of imminent monetary policy easing, while bitcoin currently lacks a clear macroeconomic catalyst that could support a rebound.

Retail investors shift their attention to tech stocks

An additional problem for the crypto market is the outflow of some retail investors toward technology stocks, especially companies linked to artificial intelligence. Retail investors have largely left the cryptocurrency market and returned to equities, making it difficult to identify new sources of demand for bitcoin.

In an environment of weakening interest and a lack of fresh capital, every negative piece of news can trigger a stronger price reaction. This applies both to macroeconomic data and to decisions by major entities holding significant bitcoin reserves.

Security issues weaken trust in Crypto

The cryptocurrency market is also struggling with concerns over trust in the security of blockchain technology. Investors paid particular attention to a vulnerability in the Zcash network, after which the cryptocurrency’s price fell by more than 40 percent in a single day. Developers fixed the bug, but they were unable to clearly determine whether it had been exploited to create additional tokens.

This situation increased concerns that increasingly advanced artificial intelligence models may in the future help detect similar vulnerabilities in other cryptocurrency projects. For a market already under downward pressure, such information further worsens sentiment.

Lack of new sources of demand makes a rebound difficult

The current sell-off in bitcoin is the result of several negative factors overlapping: strong U.S. economic data, reduced expectations for interest rate cuts, investors shifting toward technology stocks, concerns about Strategy’s future actions, trust issues related to the security of some crypto projects, and the large scale of long liquidations in the leveraged instruments market.

Bitcoin remains under pressure, and the lack of clear new sources of demand means that a quick and sustained rebound may be difficult. The market appears weakened, and investors are watching increasingly closely to see whether the drop below USD 60,000 proves to be only a brief breach of an important level or a continuation of the downward trend that began in October 2025.

data.title: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) Q3 earnings preview: GTA VI launch is the critical catalyst for TTWO
data.description:
Referenced assets

Key takeaways

  • GTA VI’s 19 November launch is the dominant catalyst, with any reaffirmation likely supportive and renewed delay risk potentially triggering sharp downside.
  • FY2027 bookings guidance and pre-order momentum matter most, as investors assess whether GTA VI can deliver the sales upside already embedded in expectations.
  • Technically, 188.65/183.86 is the key support zone, while a break above 201.44 may expose 212.16/215.66 and a broader mean-reversion rebound.

Ahead of next Monday’s earnings release, Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) faces a crucial test of investor confidence, with its highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) scheduled for release on 19 November 2026, just ten days after its fiscal second-quarter results.

Unlike most earnings announcements, the market’s attention will likely be directed less towards historical financial performance and more towards management’s confidence in its biggest upcoming game launch, the potential for record sales, and the sustainability of recurrent consumer spending.

Take-Two has confirmed that it will release its Q2 FY2027 results after the US market closes on Monday, 9 November, followed by an earnings conference call at 4:30 pm Eastern Time (5:30 am Singapore time, 10 November).

At the start of the week of 2 November 2026, the share price of Take-Two traded to a close of $192.10, languishing near its 52-week low, reflecting market concerns ahead of the game’s release and uncertainty surrounding the company’s future profitability.

Based on the street’s consensus, revenue and earnings growth are expected to be lacklustre; revenue is expected to decline 9% year-on-year to US$1.61 billion, while EPS growth is expected to slide 6.6% year-on-year to US$0.97.

Ahead of Take-Two’s Q2 FY2027 earnings release, options markets are pricing an approximately ±10.2% move in Take-Two’s shares (TTWO) as of 3 November 2026, above its 10-year average peak earnings-day movement of 8.6%, according to data from EarningsWatcher.[3]

Hence, this creates a particularly sensitive earnings setup: confirmation that GTA VI remains on schedule could support a recovery rally, while any renewed uncertainty over the release date could trigger substantial downside, given the game’s importance to Take-Two’s future revenue and earnings.

Here are the six key fundamental factors traders should monitor.

1. GTA VI release timetable: the single biggest share-price catalyst

The most important development will be whether management firmly reiterates the 19 November 2026 launch date for GTA VI, following two previous postponements.

The stakes are particularly high because the title is expected to generate billions of dollars in sales, with management’s FY2027 financial guidance incorporating its release during the current fiscal year.

Previous delays have demonstrated the stock’s sensitivity to launch uncertainty. Reuters reported that Take-Two shares fell approximately 6% following the November 2025 postponement.

2. FY2027 net bookings guidance: can GTA VI deliver a stronger earnings outlook?

Management has maintained its full-year FY2027 net bookings guidance of US$8.0 billion–US$8.2 billion, representing approximately 20% growth at the midpoint compared with FY2026.

However, Wedbush recently projected annual net bookings of US$8.605 billion, above management’s existing guidance, reflecting expectations of stronger GTA VI launch sales.

This suggests a possible gap between management’s conservative forecasts and the upside already anticipated by some investors.

The market will also examine the revenue assumptions underpinning GTA VI, including initial unit sales, game pricing, premium editions and the potential contribution from digital distribution.

3. GTA VI pre-orders and launch sales expectations: the key demand indicator

Take-Two announced that GTA VI pre-orders opened on 24 June 2026, giving investors an opportunity to assess early consumer interest ahead of the November launch.

Traders will be looking for evidence of strong pre-order momentum, particularly across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles.

Wedbush’s latest projections assume approximately 31 million units sold during the launch quarter, with a net realised price of US$62.50 per copy, supporting projected quarterly net bookings of US$3.437 billion. These are analyst assumptions, not confirmed sales or company guidance.

Such forecasts underline why GTA VI is expected to become a transformative revenue event for Take-Two.

4. NBA 2K27 and recurrent consumer spending: underlying business resilience

While GTA VI dominates investor attention, Take-Two’s existing game portfolio remains important in supporting cash generation ahead of the launch.

In Q1 FY2027, recurrent consumer spending declined 1% on a net bookings basis and accounted for 84% of total net bookings, highlighting the importance of recurring purchases from established titles.

For Q2, management previously forecast a roughly 5% decline in recurrent consumer spending, reflecting weaker mobile gaming trends despite continued growth expectations for NBA 2K and Grand Theft Auto.

Investors will monitor early demand for NBA 2K27, player engagement, virtual currency purchases and the sustainability of in-game spending.

5. Zynga mobile gaming: can profitability and bookings stabilise?

Take-Two’s mobile gaming portfolio, primarily operated through Zynga, remains another important source of recurrent revenue.

Management expects Zynga to contribute approximately 34% of FY2027 net bookings, although weaker performance among mature mobile titles and higher user acquisition costs remain key challenges.

Traders will assess whether mobile titles such as Toon Blast, Match Factory!, Empires & Puzzles and Words With Friends can maintain player engagement and spending.

Importantly, mobile gaming profitability also depends on the efficiency of customer acquisition and advertising expenditure.

6. Operating margins, cash flow and GTA VI monetisation

The final key factor is whether Take-Two can translate the anticipated surge in GTA VI revenue into sustainably higher profits and free cash flow.

Management previously guided for more than US$1 billion in FY2027 operating cash flow, while projecting approximately US$290 million in capital expenditure.

However, the game developer’s profit-sharing arrangements, marketing expenditure and ongoing development costs may absorb part of the incremental revenue generated by GTA VI.

Wedbush recently reduced its FY2029 EPS forecast to US$9.98 from US$11.19, citing a greater anticipated contribution from Rockstar Games and its staff royalty-sharing arrangements.

This highlights an important distinction between exceptionally strong game sales and the earnings ultimately attributable to Take-Two shareholders.

Fundamental bottom line: What matters most for traders

Take-Two’s earnings reaction will likely hinge on four key factors: GTA VI’s release timetable, FY2027 net bookings guidance, pre-orders and initial sales expectations, and recurring consumer spending, with the profitability outlook determining whether any post-earnings recovery can be sustained.

The bull case is clean earnings beat accompanied by management reaffirming the 19 November GTA VI launch date, stronger-than-expected demand indications and an upward revision to full-year net bookings guidance.

This would reinforce expectations of a substantial earnings recovery and potentially attract renewed buying interest following the stock’s recent weakness.

The bear case is not necessarily disappointing quarterly earnings, but renewed uncertainty over GTA VI’s launch timetable or management’s ability to convert record game sales into sustainable profitability.

Another postponement, weaker sales forecasts, or deteriorating trends in recurring consumer spending could trigger further selling pressure.

Let’s now take a deep dive into the technical analysis of Take-Two (TTWO) to decipher its medium-term (multi-week) outlook.

Technical analysis: Potential mean-reversion rebound at major range support of 183.86

The 16-week decline of 31% in Take-Two (TTWO) from its current intraday all-time high of 265.94 printed on 7 July 2025 has reached and tested a major range support of 188.65/183.86 (see Fig. 1).

There are now signs that TTWO may shape a potential mean reversion rebound towards the mid-section of a major sideways range configuration in place since 15 October 2025.

Firstly, TTWO’s price action has formed a daily bullish “Hammer” candlestick after it printed a 52-week low of 183.86 on 30 October 2026.

Secondly, the Chaikin Money Flow indicator, a combination of price and volume momentum, formed a bullish divergence condition on 2 November 2026

These observations suggest a potentially oversold condition in TTWO, with bearish momentum declining.

Watch the 188.65/183.86 key medium-term pivotal support, and a clearance above the 201.44 intermediate resistance targets the first medium-term resistance at 212.16/215.66 (also close to the 200-day moving average) in the first step.

On the other hand, a failure to hold and a daily close below 183.86 would invalidate the mean-reversion rebound scenario and trigger a potential major bearish breakdown, exposing the next medium-term supports at 169.56/162.98 and 147.23.

data.title: Apple ahead of earnings: Record sales are only the beginning of the test
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • Apple faces expectations of $113.44 billion in quarterly revenue and earnings per share of $1.99.
  • Investors will assess whether strong iPhone sales and high-margin services can offset rising costs and supply constraints.
  • John Ternus’s first earnings report as CEO will put sustainable profitability and the holiday outlook in focus.

Apple is approaching its earnings release with expectations for quarterly revenue exceeding $113 billion. Following a strong first half of the calendar year, however, investors will be looking to see how much of that sales growth translates into a sustained improvement in profitability. The previous report showed that even record results require a careful reading of the footnotes: some of the profit came from tariff refunds.

November’s report will cover the quarter ended in September

The release scheduled for November 2 will cover Apple’s fourth fiscal quarter, which ended in September. This is an important distinction: the third fiscal quarter ended on June 27 and was reported in July. The upcoming results will include initial sales of the iPhone 18 Pro, while the October launch of the iPhone Duo will affect the following reporting period. Management’s commentary on the holiday season could therefore prove just as important as the historical figures.

The market expects revenue of more than $113 billion - tariff refunds boosted previous quarter

The analyst consensus calls for revenue of $113.44 billion and earnings per share of $1.99. That would represent year-over-year growth of approximately 10.7% and 7.6%, respectively. Apple’s management previously guided for quarterly revenue growth of 9–11% and a gross margin of 47–48%. Based on last year’s revenue of $102.47 billion, a simple calculation puts the implied revenue range at approximately $111.7–113.7 billion. The market forecast therefore sits near the upper end of that range. This raises the bar: meeting management’s guidance will not necessarily deliver a positive surprise for investors.

The record June quarter remains the benchmark. Apple generated approximately $109.4 billion in revenue, with diluted earnings per share of $2.02. However, the company disclosed that tariff refunds boosted earnings per share by 11 cents and gross margin by approximately 2 percentage points. Simply subtracting those benefits gives earnings per share of $1.91 and a gross margin of approximately 48.1%.

iPhone drives sales, but development is becoming more expensive

Sales were driven primarily by the iPhone, whose quarterly revenue rose approximately 22% to $54.25 billion. The Mac also performed strongly, with revenue increasing approximately 29% to $10.35 billion. Services generated $30.74 billion, up approximately 12% year over year. Their importance extends beyond revenue, however: the services gross margin was 75.6%, compared with 40.1% for products. This means the revenue mix has a significant impact on the company’s overall profitability.

At the same time, Apple must fund increasingly expensive development efforts. In the latest quarter, research and development spending rose 32% to $11.73 billion, while total operating expenses increased 23% to $19.08 billion. Both therefore grew faster than revenue. A key question in assessing the next set of results will be whether higher sales and a more favorable contribution from services are enough to cover rising expenditure.

Component availability remains a separate challenge. Speaking to Reuters after the July report, Tim Cook pointed to constraints on advanced chip production capacity. Memory costs also added pressure on profitability. This calls for caution when interpreting sales figures: an inability to deliver devices to willing buyers has different implications for the company’s future than weakening demand, even though both can limit revenue in the short term.

Apple shares closed at $347.10 on October 27, having reached an all-time high of $351.73 just two trading sessions earlier. The earnings release could determine whether the trend continues or investors shift into profit-taking mode. AAPL shares have gained more than 27.49% since the start of 2026.

John Ternus prepares for his first earnings report as CEO

The upcoming report will also be the first under John Ternus, who became Apple’s CEO on September 1. Tim Cook moved into the role of executive chairman of the board. The new leadership will therefore present the company’s outlook at a time when strong hardware sales are accompanied by rising costs and supply constraints. The most important test for Apple will be whether its improving results can be sustained. Beating the consensus by a few cents per share will say less than stable margins without one-off benefits, continued services growth, and the ability to deliver new devices during the holiday season. These factors will help determine whether the record June quarter signals a longer period of earnings growth.

data.title: Fed and ECB: a pause before further tightening
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • The Fed and ECB are likely to hold rates steady in October, while keeping December hikes on the table.
  • Persistent inflation and resilient growth support further monetary tightening.
  • French bond market tensions could constrain the ECB’s room to raise rates.
  • Lower energy prices and tighter financing conditions could reduce the need for additional hikes next year.
  • Central bank guidance will shape bond yields, while French fiscal risks could weigh on the euro.

The Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank are likely to leave interest rates unchanged at their October meetings. However, a pause would not necessarily mark the end of monetary tightening. Persistent inflation and resilient economic activity support the case for further increases in December, although tensions in the French government bond market could constrain the ECB.

Inflation remains too high

Price pressures on both sides of the Atlantic remain too strong for central banks to declare victory. In the US, annual PCE inflation stood at 3.4% in August, while the core measure reached 3.0%. In the euro area, headline inflation rose to 3.8%, with core inflation at 2.5%.

The risk that higher energy costs will feed through to other goods and services continues to complicate the return to target. Meanwhile, relatively resilient economic activity reduces the likelihood that weaker demand alone will quickly contain inflation.

The forecasts presented in the source material point to annualised US GDP growth of 3.5% in the third quarter and quarterly growth of 0.3% in the euro area. Such readings would give policymakers additional room to maintain a restrictive stance.

October favours caution

Despite these inflation risks, recent central bank communication suggests that caution will prevail in October. Following September’s rate increases, policymakers have reasons to assess their effects before taking further action. Geopolitical uncertainty and higher government bond yields also strengthen the case for a pause.

For the Federal Reserve, the proximity of the US midterm elections adds political sensitivity to the upcoming meeting. This could reinforce the appeal of waiting, although the inflation outlook remains the central consideration.

French debt tensions complicate the ECB’s decision

France presents an additional challenge for the ECB. The spread between French and German ten-year government bond yields has approached 175 basis points, reflecting concerns about public finances and the government’s ability to deliver fiscal consolidation.

Another rapid rate increase could raise borrowing costs further and intensify market tensions. A December hike therefore remains conditional on the French debt market avoiding a more serious deterioration.

December hikes remain the base case

A further 25 - basis - point increase by both central banks in December remains the base case. The outlook for additional tightening next year is less clear.

A normalisation of oil supplies from the Middle East could lower energy prices and gradually ease inflation. At the same time, elevated long - term bond yields are already tightening financing conditions, potentially reducing the need for further policy rate increases.

Guidance will shape the market response

Markets will focus on the guidance accompanying any October pause. A clear signal that December hikes remain on the table could limit declines in short-term bond yields.

For the euro, however, monetary policy expectations are only part of the picture. A further deterioration in French public finances could weigh on the currency even if the ECB maintains a hawkish message.

EUR/USD: Downtrend channel remains intact

There is no doubt that EUR/USD has been trading within a descending channel since February 2026. The latest upward correction ended around 1.1279, and the pair is now moving lower again. The pattern of lower highs and lower lows confirms that sellers remain in control.

The nearest support lies at 1.1115, last week’s low. A break below this level could pave the way towards the channel’s lower boundary, near 1.1000. Conversely, a recovery above 1.1279 could allow the correction to extend towards the 1.1340 area.
